title: Rust Beginner Mock Test 2
description: Comprehensive 50-minute mock examination for Rust at beginner level.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest beginner application of Cargo?

options.text: use cargo check test and run as separate evidence
Cargo builds tests and manages crate metadata
Cargo.lock policy differs between applications and libraries
The compiler silently repairs the design

questions.explanation: use cargo check test and run as separate evidence. Confirm with cargo check, Clippy, and a focused test.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest beginner application of rustfmt?

options.text: run cargo fmt before review
rustfmt applies canonical formatting
manual formatting drift distracts from behavior
The compiler silently repairs the design

questions.explanation: run cargo fmt before review. Confirm with cargo check, Clippy, and a focused test.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest beginner application of Clippy?

options.text: review each lint in its code context
Clippy provides additional lint diagnostics
blindly allowing lints can hide defects
The compiler silently repairs the design

questions.explanation: review each lint in its code context. Confirm with cargo check, Clippy, and a focused test.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest beginner application of immutability?

options.text: request mutability only where state changes
bindings are immutable unless marked mut
interior mutability follows separate runtime rules
The compiler silently repairs the design

questions.explanation: request mutability only where state changes. Confirm with cargo check, Clippy, and a focused test.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest beginner application of String and str?

options.text: accept &str for read-only text parameters
String owns text while str slices borrow text
byte indexing is unavailable because UTF-8 boundaries matter
The compiler silently repairs the design

questions.explanation: accept &str for read-only text parameters. Confirm with cargo check, Clippy, and a focused test.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest beginner application of Option?

options.text: match or transform both possibilities intentionally
Option models presence with Some or absence with None
unwrap can panic when absence is possible
The compiler silently repairs the design

questions.explanation: match or transform both possibilities intentionally. Confirm with cargo check, Clippy, and a focused test.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest beginner application of Result?

options.text: propagate or handle errors before using output

ignoring an Err loses required control flow
The compiler silently repairs the design

questions.explanation: propagate or handle errors before using output. Confirm with cargo check, Clippy, and a focused test.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest beginner application of question mark?

options.text: use it in compatible Result or Option functions

The compiler silently repairs the design

questions.explanation: use it in compatible Result or Option functions. Confirm with cargo check, Clippy, and a focused test.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest beginner application of match?

options.text: enumerate domain variants explicitly

a wildcard can hide newly added variants
The compiler silently repairs the design

questions.explanation: enumerate domain variants explicitly. Confirm with cargo check, Clippy, and a focused test.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest beginner application of ranges?

options.text: use inclusive syntax when the endpoint belongs
exclusive ranges omit their upper endpoint

The compiler silently repairs the design

questions.explanation: use inclusive syntax when the endpoint belongs. Confirm with cargo check, Clippy, and a focused test.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest beginner application of iterators?

options.text: consume with collect sum or a loop

building a chain alone may perform no work
The compiler silently repairs the design

questions.explanation: consume with collect sum or a loop. Confirm with cargo check, Clippy, and a focused test.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest beginner application of ownership?

options.text: move values deliberately across boundaries

The compiler silently repairs the design

questions.explanation: move values deliberately across boundaries. Confirm with cargo check, Clippy, and a focused test.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest beginner application of shared borrowing?

options.text: use &T for temporary read-only borrowing

The compiler silently repairs the design

questions.explanation: use &T for temporary read-only borrowing. Confirm with cargo check, Clippy, and a focused test.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest beginner application of mutable borrowing?

options.text: keep mutable borrow scope as short as practical

questions.explanation: keep mutable borrow scope as short as practical. Confirm with cargo check, Clippy, and a focused test.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest beginner application of slices?

The compiler silently repairs the design

questions.explanation: accept slices instead of requiring Vec ownership. Confirm with cargo check, Clippy, and a focused test.
